summary: Enforce Slack channel naming standards + auto-create Confluence backlinking bot for new project spaces
description: Issue summary: We need an automated workflow that enforces Slack channel naming conventions at creation time and stitches a persistent backlink from the created Slack channel to the corresponding Confluence space (and vice versa). Background: multiple pods are creating ad-hoc Slack channels and Confluence spaces with inconsistent names and missing links. This leads to discovery problems, accidental duplicate spaces, and increased audit/retention overhead. Request: 1) Implement a Slack Channel Creation webhook + enforcement bot that validates channel names against our naming policy (pod-<team>-<purpose>-<env>) and offers a suggested corrected name if the creator's proposed name fails validation. 2) If the creator has the appropriate role, allow the bot to auto-rename (with consent flow) or queue the request for approver review. 3) When a new Confluence space is created via our project bootstrap flow, automatically post a canonical link into the newly created Slack channel and update the Confluence space home page with the Slack channel link. 4) Ensure Okta group membership is used to determine approvers for auto-rename and that all actions are logged to the audit channel and a Confluence change-log page. Why now: growth in ephemeral channels plus recent audit requests from Security require better linkage and predictable naming to support retention and e-discovery. Constraints: minimal disruption to existing automated provisioning; any rename must preserve message history and avoid breaking incoming webhooks. Non-goal: this ticket is not intended to implement a full archival sweep (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Slack creation webhook validates channel name format and returns clear guidance to the user within 30s
If user consents and has approver role, bot performs an auto-rename and posts confirmation; otherwise request appears in an approver queue
New Confluence spaces created via the project bootstrap pipeline contain a prominent Slack channel link on the space home and the Slack channel has a pinned Confluence space link
All rename and link actions are logged to #infra-audit with a timestamp and Okta user id
Documentation and a short runbook for support are published in Confluence and linked in the ticket
